newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russian statistics official sees '98 GDP growth.
newsitem.headline: Russian statistics official sees '98 GDP growth.

text.p: The Russian economy will see real growth in 1998, a deputy chairman of the State Statistics Committee said on Friday.

"I think today we can say with a high degree of certainty that the beginning of growth now being forecast for the Russian economy next year will happen," said Vladimir Sokolin, deputy chairman of the State Committe for Statistics.
He did not comment on annual growth for 1997 although government officials have said gross domestic product (GDP) would increase by two percent.
But Sokolin said economic growth was currently flat.
"What we are observing now is a fairly stable -- and that is a new phenomenon at the beginning of the year -- GDP indicator in the region of 100 percent," he said.
By Russian standards, a GDP indicator of 100 percent shows the economy stable -- neither growing nor falling.

"As for March and April, around a breakthrough period there are always periods -- say three, four, five or six months -- when a certain movement can be observed. It might be more than 100 percent, it might be a little less, but it will be in the region of 100 percent."

Sokolin said the Committee would stand by January and February year-on-year growth rates of 0.1 and 0.9 percent which have been criticised but added those figures did not indicate real growth, which he defined as about 5-6 percent annually.
Russian GDP fell by six percent in 1996, the committee said.
